messages:
sanjay: FYI POC with AcmeHealth hitting repeated 429s + ECONNRESET when running behind their corporate proxy. Started after we ramped concurrency for a demo. Logs below.

sanjay: raw logs pasted: 
```
2026-03-18T14:10:01Z ERROR client.py HTTPError 429 Too Many Requests
2026-03-18T14:10:01Z WARN urllib3.connectionpool ReadTimeoutError: HTTPConnectionPool(host='proxy.corp', port=8080): Read timed out. (read timeout=10)
2026-03-18T14:10:02Z ERROR transport.py Proxy auth required: 407 Proxy Authentication Required
```

ethan: Can you paste the SDK client init they're using? Are they relying on env proxy vars (requests default)? @maria-sale any constraints on asking them to open direct egress for the POC?

maria-sale: They will not allow direct egress. Security insisted all traffic must go via internal proxy. Pricing is fine; they just need the security questionnaire answered.

olivia-support: This pattern often means the proxy is returning 407/NTLM which causes the SDK to retry sockets, and our hosted pool sees spikes -> 429s. Two angles: (1) fix client connection pooling/retries so requests queue instead of opening new connections, (2) address proxy auth/NTLM handshake.

ethan: Quick Python suggestion (non-invasive): reduce concurrency and set pool_block so requests wait for a free connection instead of creating new ones. Example patch for the Python client config: 
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED", transport_opts={
  "max_connections": 10,
  "pool_block": True,        # queue instead of spawn sockets
  "timeout": (3.05, 30),
  "retries": {"total": 5, "backoff_factor": 0.7}
}, http_proxy="http://proxy.corp:8080", trust_env=False)
```
Also set the app-level concurrency to 4 for the POC.

sanjay: They're on Windows and their proxy is NTLM. They can't share proxy creds with us.

kevin-security: If it's NTLM we can't accept customers forwarding credentials to us. Best practice: customer provides an egress/bastion that terminates NTLM and performs outbound TLS to our endpoints with mutual TLS or an allowlisted IP. For short POCs we can accept a temporary allowlist + audit log.

maria-sale: I'll queue the SOC + network questionnaire items and push to them today.

olivia-support: For NTLM dev hack only: requests-ntlm or requests-negotiate-sspi works on Windows, but not acceptable for production. If they do that for test, make sure to enable client-side rate limiting/backoff.

ethan: Note also TLS interception makes keepalive/connection pooling brittle. If their proxy does MITM and reuses a new backend connection per request, pooling won't help. Confirm whether proxy preserves keepalive.

sanjay: I ran a local curl repro and got 407: 
```
curl -x http://proxy.corp:8080 -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
```

olivia-support: Next steps from support side: provide a tiny diagnostic script that exercises pooling, records response headers (via Connection and Proxy-Authenticate), and captures timing. I'll paste it in this thread.

ethan: Immediate mitigations we can recommend to the customer: 
- throttle concurrent client workers to 3-4
- enable pool_block (so clients queue)
- implement exponential backoff with jitter
- temporarily use a Dedicated sandbox (reduces shared rate-limit surface)

kevin-security: I'm ok with a short-lived egress allowlist if they provide justification and we get SOC answers. @maria-sale pls attach the questionnaire.

maria-sale: Will do. Also they requested a Dedicated trial quote — ethan, can you produce a small commit-level quote for a 2-week sandbox?

ethan: I can spin up a tiny dedicated pod for the POC — will get pricing to you within an hour.

sanjay: Action items: 
- sanjay: ask customer to set client max concurrency=4, pool_block=True, retries/backoff
- ethan: prepare Dedicated sandbox quote + small playbook
- kevin-security: review short-lived egress allowlist process
- olivia-support: send diagnostic script + runbook for capturing proxy headers and tcpdump

deploy-bot: Ticket #3287 created: sales/poc/3287 — attach logs and next steps.

sanjay: Thanks all — I'll push the config to the customer and update thread after their test. :thumbsup:

olivia-support: If they still see 407/429 after config change, capture tcpdump + proxy logs and drop them here. I'll help analyze.

(END OF THREAD)
